slo_title: Implement the concept of Dynamic Memory Allocation

mcq.q: How does dynamic memory allocation improve memory utilization in C programs?

options.A: By increasing the size of static arrays
options.B: By allocating memory at compile time
options.C: By allocating memory during runtime as needed

mcq.answer_text: By allocating memory during runtime as needed

mcq.q: Given a structure in C, how would you dynamically allocate memory for an array of 10 such structures

options.B: struct myStruct* arr = (struct myStruct*)malloc(10 * sizeof(struct myStruct));
options.D: struct myStruct arr = malloc(10 * sizeof(struct myStruct));

mcq.answer_text: struct myStruct* arr = (struct myStruct*)malloc(10 * sizeof(struct myStruct));

The concept of dynamic memory allocation in c language enables the C programmer to allocate memory at runtime. Dynamic memory allocation in c language is possible by 4 functions of stdlib.h header file.
Before learning above functions, let's understand the difference between static memory allocation and dynamic memory allocation.
Memory is allocated at compile time.
Memory is allocated at run time.
Memory can't be increased while executing program.
Memory can be increased while executing program.

Allocates single block of requested memory.
Allocates multiple block of requested memory.
